title: Renderer neutrality: Web, Swing, GTK/Direct Linux and Android must agree
summary: All first-class renderers implement one Wire semantic contract. Native presentation may differ, but exact identities, revisions, semantic actions, bounded demand, resource authority, observation/subscription meaning and fail-closed behaviour must not drift.
invariants: Do not fork journey, business, security, resource or observation semantics by renderer.
Exact definitionId@version and event-time renderedRevision have one meaning on every renderer.
Virtual collections select/activate by stable application identity; row ordinal is never semantic identity.
Bounded virtual demand is RangeRequested(start,count); renderer reports need, application/source authority decides what data to project.
Workspace-bound actions carry exact opaque server-projected workspaceContext captured at the same event-time boundary as renderedRevision.
Required customer-facing resources are exact published ResourceRefs; renderers must not invent labels, URLs or copy.
Renderer-owned styling, including Swing chips or GTK/Android presentation choices, must not create or deny semantic actions.
A renderer is conformant only when a real adapter emits the canonical normalized transcript and the comparator passes.

provenance.claim: 59/59 dev11 presentation regression; semantic baseline retained from dev10 including RangeRequested/workspace context.
Renderer-neutral semantic UI proxy and semantic activation.
Stable application identity and renderer-neutral roundtrip.
Explicit no-drift doctrine across GTK/Linux, Android, Web/Swing and Windows.
